extracted.intended_audience: readers and policymakers interested in public finance and the French Revolution (late-18th-century British public/political class)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and normative statements for judging the conduct of national financial management (revenue, taxation, credit, and confiscation) as discussed in a political/financial critique of revolutionary France.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of a financier
rubrics_metrics.description: “The objects of a financier are, then, to secure an ample revenue; to impose it with judgment and equality; to employ it economically; and when necessity obliges him to make use of credit, to secure its foundations in that instance, and forever, by the clearness and candor of his proceedings, the exactness of his calculations, and the solidity of his funds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single statement is presented as the canonical checklist for sound public finance: ample revenue; fair and judicious imposition; economical expenditure; and, when using credit, transparent accounts, precise calculation, and solid funding. The rest of the essay evaluates the Assembly against these four linked duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure an ample revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue must be adequate to the state's needs; 'the revenue of the state is the state' — all public action depends on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A financer should ensure receipts are sufficient for support and reformation of the state. Diminution of revenue (e.g., the reported loss of two hundred millions) is judged as catastrophic, undermining every other public virtue and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose taxes with judgment and equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes should be imposed 'with judgment and equality', proportioned to citizens' means and least likely to burden productive capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid schemes that let districts or individuals opt out (leading to new oppressive inequalities). Do not concentrate the burden on the most submissive or orderly provinces; distribution must be fair to preserve production and public spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ revenue economically (economy in expenditures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public funds must be used economically; reduction of prodigal expenses is a principal measure of financial prudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare present expenses (National Assembly, municipalities, armies, police, pensions, new judicatures) with revenues; mere rhetoric of economy is insufficient if the new system’s outlays exceed the treasury’s capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: When using credit, ensure clearness, candor, and exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: When the state resorts to credit, it must secure foundations by clear and candid accounts, exact calculations, and solid funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit must be based on trustworthy, transparent evidence of security (value of property, incumbrances, net surplus) so purchasers and creditors know precisely what they buy; otherwise credit collapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and authentic valuation before issuing secured paper (assignats/land-bank)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing paper backed by confiscated property, provide a rent-roll, inventory, gross value, charges, incumbrances, net surplus, and clear statements of time/conditions of sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text insists on methodical business-like procedures: ascertain gross value, management charges, all incumbrances, strike a net surplus, vest it with trustees, indicate parcels/time/conditions of sale, then admit public subscription. Failure to do so brands the fund as fraudulent and undermines credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not destroy settled revenue to rebuild on confiscated property
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reckless to dismantle established revenue systems in the hope of rebuilding public credit on confiscations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay condemns replacing reliable revenue streams with temporary or speculative resources (church confiscations) that cannot reliably underwrite public credit or long-term supplies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on 'benevolences' and patriotic donations as sustainable taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary contributions (a 'fourth part of the income' by honor or 'patriotic donations') are weak, unequal, and unreliable sources of public revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benevolences tend to be ineffective, screen luxury and selfishness, place burden on productive capital, and may ultimately require coercion; they are not substitutes for regular, equal taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not issue unbacked paper currency; ensure convertibility and specie backing
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper money (assignats) must be founded on cash deposits or on clear, convertible backing; paper without legal convertibility or real backing will depreciate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with Bank of England notes that are convertible and arise from deposited cash; the Assembly’s assignats depreciated immediately because they lacked specie backing and convertibility, causing market depreciation and undermining receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require treasury receipts in specie or equivalent to prevent loss from depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasury should, where necessary, require collectors to pay in the specie they received rather than accept depreciated paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting depreciated paper (when collectors receive coin and account in depreciated paper) creates arbitrage/profit for collectors and losses for the Treasury; insisting on specie helps protect public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for all charges when using confiscated estates as security
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriating Church or other property, account for the costs of maintaining establishments, pensions, and municipal management — these charges can exceed income from the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confiscation does not eliminate charges (support of ministers, relief of the poor, pensions, management expenses). Failing to account for these makes the apparent security unsound and can leave an uncovered deficit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare and state clearly public expenditures against revenue (full accounting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce clear statements of public charges for each year and compare the aggregate of general and municipal establishments with regular income by revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assembly had pledged to show sums necessary for religious/support charges and failed to furnish such statements; without full accounting the nation cannot judge solvency of proposed measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ideological or metaphysical financial schemes; prefer business-like, economical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial policy must be grounded in practical economic principles, not in philosophical enthusiasm or metaphysical remedies (e.g., assigning infinite efficacy to confiscation or 'philosophic' cures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay ridicules schemes born of 'philosophy'—e.g., faith in sacrilege, coining church bells—and warns that such fantasies produce ruinous consequences. Practical examples and historical commercial reasoning should guide policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not coerce creditors or foreign merchants by force or arbitrary terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A government that dictates terms by force (discharging one engagement with another, prescribing medium of solvency at bayonet-point) will not attract foreign lenders or merchants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign nations and commercial centers will deal only with solvent, credible borrowers; coercive or arbitrary financial behavior destroys international credit relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repeated emissions of new paper as the cure for depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing new paper to remedy depreciation of earlier paper (e.g., 'Are old assignats depreciated? Issue new assignats') is a vicious cycle that deepens distrust and depreciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticizes the reflex of issuing more assignats as the sole remedy; experience shows repeated emissions simply increase depreciation and fail to resolve underlying insolvency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use sacrilegious or short-term plunder as lasting financial policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Plundering Church plate and private effects is an unreliable, short-lived device; it may yield temporary supplies but destroys perennial sources and public morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay labels such measures 'servile imitation' of despotic tactics and warns they will exhaust resources and fail as a permanent foundation for the state’s finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explicit time/conditions and trustee arrangements when mortgaging land as security
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating a land-bank or mortgage-based fund, explicitly indicate the parcels to be sold, the time and conditions of sale, and properly vest net surplus in trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of conducting the enterprise 'like men of business' so that dealers/investors know exactly what they purchase and the security’s nature is credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of fiscal measures that redistribute burdens unfairly through local discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing districts or individuals to judge what old revenues they may withhold introduces new, oppressive inequalities, as compliant regions end up bearing disproportionate burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized, principled allocation is necessary; leaving distribution to local discretion transforms reform into opportunistic exemption and unfair tax incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critically assess short-term relief touted as benefit to the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept political claims that destruction of public revenue or confiscation constitutes relief to the people without analyzing who bears costs and who gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay insists on evaluating whether paying more and gaining proportionally is preferable to paying little and losing public services — historical experience favors stable contributions that sustain public goods.
